facts.statement: The genus Siroccopteryx was named and described in 1999 by paleontologists Bryn Mader and Alexander Kellner.
facts.quote: The genus was named and described in 1999 by Bryn Mader and Alexander Kellner.

facts.statement: The name Siroccopteryx means "wing of the Sirocco," combining a reference to the North African wind with the Greek word for wing.
facts.quote: The name Siroccopteryx means "wing of the Sirocco", referring to the warm wind that originates in the North Africa and then goes through the Mediterranean, and the Greek word pteryx, a standard suffix for pterosaur genera that means "wing".

facts.statement: The species name moroccensis indicates that the animal was found in Morocco.
facts.quote: The epithet of the type species S. moroccensis refers to its country of origin.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil LINHM 016 was discovered in southeastern Morocco within red sandstone layers dating from the Albian to Cenomanian stages.
facts.quote: The holotype fossil, LINHM 016 (Long Island Natural History Museum), was found near Ksar es Souk, in the province of Errachidia in the region of Meknes-Tafilalet at 30.4 ° N, 4.9 ° longitude (17.6 ° N, 4.2 ° W longitude) in Beg'aa, west of Hamada du Guiren in southeastern Morocco, in a layer of red sandstone, a fine-grained alluvium from the Albian to Cenomanian.

facts.statement: Siroccopteryx had a long, narrow muzzle with a large terminal part and an anterior keel crest that was higher than Anhanguera's but lower than Coloborhynchus or Tropeognathus.
facts.quote: The muzzle was long and narrow, with a large elongated terminal part, along with some sort of crest shaped anterior keel higher than that of Anhanguera but not as high as that of Coloborhynchus or Tropeognathus.

facts.statement: The teeth of Siroccopteryx were sharp, short, and more robust than those of Anhanguera.
facts.quote: The teeth were sharp but short and more robust than in Anhanguera.

facts.statement: The fossil bone surface is rough and leathery with wrinkles and depressions that some researchers suggest indicate a disease like dental abscesses.
facts.quote: The bone is rough and leathery, with strange marks of wrinkles and depressions, this may be a consequence of the conditions of preservation, but the descriptors suggest that it indicates a disease, possibly caused by dental abscesses.

facts.statement: Researcher André Veldmeijer suggests that the wrinkles and depressions on the bone likely indicate a keratinous cover on the ridge rather than disease.
facts.quote: According to André Veldmeijer, it is probable that this damage was post-mortem and that it indicates the presence of a keratinous cover on the ridge.

facts.statement: Siroccopteryx had an estimated wingspan of 4 to 5 meters.
facts.quote: The wingspan of this large pterosaur was estimated to be 4 to 5 m.

facts.statement: Siroccopteryx is classified as an extinct anhanguerid pterodactyloid pterosaur.
facts.quote: Siroccopteryx is an extinct genus of anhanguerid pterodactyloid pterosaur which lived in Morocco during the Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Siroccopteryx lived in Morocco during the Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Siroccopteryx is an extinct genus of anhanguerid pterodactyloid pterosaur which lived in Morocco during the Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Some researchers classify Siroccopteryx as a member of the family Ornithocheiridae.
facts.quote: Siroccopteryx es un género extinto de pterosaurio pterodactiloide de la familia Ornithocheiridae, que vivió a finales del período Cretácico Inferior (entre el Albiense y el Cenomaniense, hace cerca de 105 millones de años).

facts.statement: Siroccopteryx lived during the Late Cretaceous, between the Albian and Cenomanian stages, approximately 105 million years ago.
facts.quote: Siroccopteryx es un género extinto de pterosaurio pterodactiloide de la familia Ornithocheiridae, que vivió a finales del período Cretácico Inferior (entre el Albiense y el Cenomaniense, hace cerca de 105 millones de años).

facts.statement: Some researchers, including David M. Unwin, consider Siroccopteryx to be a junior synonym of the genus Coloborhynchus.
facts.quote: Some researchers, such as David M. Unwin, consider the genus a junior synonym of Coloborhynchus.

facts.statement: A 2018 study by Longrich et al. assigned Siroccopteryx to the family Ornithocheiridae as the sister taxon of Coloborhynchus.
facts.quote: In 2018, a topology recovered by Longrich et al. assigned Siroccopteryx to the family Ornithocheiridae as the sister taxon of Coloborhynchus.

facts.statement: A 2019 analysis by Jacobs et al. placed Siroccopteryx in Ornithocheiridae but as a sister taxon to Ornithocheirus and Tropeognathus, contradicting other studies linking it to Coloborhynchus.
facts.quote: In 2019 however, Jacobs et al. published an analysis that also recovers Siroccopteryx within the family Ornithocheiridae, but they concluded that it would have been more closely related to, and therefore the sister taxon of both Ornithocheirus and Tropeognathus, which contradicts the conclusion of Siroccopteryx being more closely related to Coloborhynchus.

facts.statement: A 2020 study by Holgado and Pêgas recovered Siroccopteryx as the sister taxon to Tropeognathus but assigned both to the family Anhangueridae.
facts.quote: In 2020, a study made by Borja Holgado and Rubi Pêgas again recovered Siroccopteryx as the sister taxon to Tropeognathus, however, they assigned both genera to the family Anhangueridae instead of the Ornithocheiridae.

facts.statement: The original describers placed Siroccopteryx in the family Anhangueridae.
facts.quote: Los descubridores de Siroccopteryx situaron a este género en la familia Anhangueridae, sensu Kellner.

facts.statement: David Unwin suggested in 2001 that Siroccopteryx was a species of Coloborhynchus, a view that has been controversial.
facts.quote: David Unwin, sin embargo, indicó en 2001 que era una especie del género Coloborhynchus, denominándose entonces C. moroccensis y siendo un miembro de los Ornithocheiridae. Esto ha sido controversial.

facts.statement: In 2009, Kellner suggested that Siroccopteryx, Coloborhynchus clavirostris, and Uktenadactylus formed a clade within Anhangueridae.
facts.quote: En 2009, Kellner consideró que Siroccopteryx, Coloborhynchus clavirostris y Uktenadactylus probablemente formaban juntos un clado dentro de Anhangueridae.
